summary.headline: Amagi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 437 crore, a record, with adjusted EBITDA margin up to 11.5% from 5%.
summary.overview: Revenue hit a record INR 437 crore, up 32% reported and 21% in constant currency, and almost 10% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose 201% YoY to INR 50 crore (11.5% margin) and PAT rose to INR 34 crore (7.5% margin), helped by a one-time non-cash FX charge of about INR 6 crore. Gross margin fell 2.2 points YoY to 67.3% on live-event mix, pricing and the prior-year base effect, though it rose about 0.5 point sequentially. Management said the Q2 YoY comparison carries a roughly 600 bps headwind from a prior-year revenue recognition benefit.

financial_highlights.change: +32% YoY reported, +21% constant currency, almost +10% QoQ
from INR 17 crore (5% margin) YoY; margin +1.2 pts QoQ

segments.name: Streaming Unification
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 249 crore, up 39% YoY, driven by existing-customer expansion and channel deliveries of almost 10,000 with distributor count at 451.

segments.name: Monetization and Marketplace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 crore, up 30% YoY, volume-driven; monetized ad impressions hit a record 13.6 billion, up 59% YoY and 21% QoQ.

segments.name: Cloud Modernization
segments.commentary: Reported growth 17% due to prior-year rev rec benefit from a large deal; management said growth would have been about 32% excluding it.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected in a 67% to 69% range for this year, treated as a base case; management says Q3 is seasonally strong.
Management focuses on full-year profitability rather than quarterly margins; H1 in FY26 was about 47% of FY revenue and about 37% of FY adjusted EBITDA (historical context, not guidance).
Q2 YoY revenue comparison carries about 600 bps headwind from prior-year rev rec timing benefit; next quarter may not be the best marker of growth.
A broader AI product suite is planned for launch at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27.
AI product revenue contribution expected mainly later in FY27, after a gestation period.
capex_capacity: Cloud cost optimisation generated about $282,000 monthly run-rate gross margin savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives.
Q1 cash outflows seasonally weakest due to annual incentives, increments and software renewals; expected to recur every Q1.
Inorganic: since January, 33 opportunities evaluated, 23 passed on, 10 under active evaluation; capability-led, focused on media industry cloud vision; no binding commitments.
Operating cash outflow excluding one-time items narrowed by INR 43 crore to INR 41 crore from INR 84 crore; one-time items about INR 25 crore this year vs INR 57 crore last year.
demand_pricing: Content processed reached 959,000 hours, up about 43% YoY; 9,900+ delivery endpoints; 451 distributors, up 21%.
Ad impressions 13.6 billion, up 59% YoY; management said FIFA did not add ad insertion upside and growth is organic (CTV penetration).
Pricing adjusted only when volume run-rate clearly outweighs price trade-off; one customer tracking more than 30% run-rate growth after pricing adjustment.
AI monetisation approached via AI credits model (cost-plus style) and telemetry to measure customer savings; outcome-based pricing seen as future option.
Management sees no material AI deflationary impact on revenue or pipeline yet; 10+ active AI pilots and a major US news network selected Newspulse.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the sequential gross margin improvement, and will margins return to 69%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides 67% to 69% for this year; gross margin was about 64% three to four years ago. AI is expected to dip margins initially on an S-curve over 2 to 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is in-sourcing by platforms a risk to ad insertion revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said platforms are outsourcing rather than in-sourcing and it is not aware of any in-sourcing impact; channel-count runway is not a fixed limit.

qa_highlights.question: Is GRR disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Not disclosed as routine; logo churn is in low single digits and top-10 customer average vintage is about 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the prior-year one-off add to growth, and what is the trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior-year base effect would have added about 4.5 percentage points to both reported and constant-currency growth; Q2 will still lap a base effect.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being priced?
qa_highlights.answer: An AI credits model mirrors cost-plus; management says it needs a few more quarters for clarity on the business model.

qa_highlights.question: What share of growth comes from existing customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to NRR as proxy: of about 31% total growth, roughly 26 points come from existing customers. NRR TTM is 125% in reported currency.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from live-event mix, customer pricing and AI costs; 67.3% in Q1 vs 69% target.
Q2 FY27 faces about 600 bps YoY base headwind from prior-year rev rec benefit.
Operating cash outflow still INR 65 crore in Q1; DSO improvement needed.
AI revenue monetisation unclear; products to be launched in Q2 with revenue visibility late FY27.
Cash deployment via M&A (10 opportunities under evaluation) could affect the INR 1,616 crore balance.
Q1 PAT includes a one-time non-cash FX charge of about INR 6 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, operating leverage and AI direction, with repeated caveats that AI is early and revenue impact is not yet visible. Cautious on gross margin and cash burn, which management framed as seasonal and full-year issues. Some answers on GRR, channel deliveries and AI pricing were deflected as not tracked.
key_quotes: Adjusted EBITDA coming in at 11.5% margin, above the FY26 full year margin of 10.3% is a data point on how the operating leverage is playing out.
So I would kind of just keep stable as your sort of base case, right?
This is not a pullback, right? It's just operating leverage.
The NRR is reported currency, Rishi.

growth.why: Q1 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 437 crore with management aspiring to sustain growth rates, but no revenue guidance number was given; the only explicit guidance is a 67-69% gross margin range, and backing is volume-led demand plus a planned AI suite without capacity or order figures.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin was 67.3% in Q1 (-2.2 pts YoY, +0.5 pt QoQ) against a 67-69% full-year range, and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 11.5% from 5% YoY, but AI is expected to dip margins initially on an S-curve over 2-4 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 32% YoY to INR 437 crore, content processed rose about 43% to 959,000 hours, and distributors rose 21% to 451, though Q2 faces a roughly 600 bps prior-year revenue recognition headwind.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue guidance number was given; the only explicit guidance is a 67-69% gross margin range, and management framed Q2 as a weaker YoY marker because of the 600 bps base headwind.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin at 67.3% sits at the bottom of the 67-69% range and AI costs could push it lower, while Q1 operating cash outflow was still INR 65 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A broader AI product suite is planned for launch at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27, though AI revenue contribution is expected mainly later in FY27 after a gestation period.

rows.label: AI product revenue ramp
rows.why: Management expects AI revenue mainly later in FY27 after a gestation period, with 10+ active AI pilots and a major US news network selected for Newspulse, but no revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Inorganic acquisitions
rows.why: Of 33 opportunities evaluated since January, 10 are under active evaluation against INR 1,616 crore cash, but there are no binding commitments.

rows.label: Cash burn narrowing
rows.why: Operating cash outflow narrowed to INR 65 crore from INR 141 crore YoY and DSO improved about 8 days QoQ, though Q1 is seasonally weakest.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, operating leverage and AI direction but cautious on gross margin and cash burn, which it framed as seasonal; analysts probed gross margin sustainability, AI in-sourcing and pricing, and some GRR and channel questions were deflected.
